text:
sara: flagging customer reports: hourly usage in Console lagging by ~3-5h for a subset of tenants. noticed after last night's patch/backfill run. anyone else seeing it?
eli: yep, saw alerts this AM. realtime ingestion looks normal, but hourly rollups show a hole and then a slow tail.
maria: pulled consumer metrics — consumer group `usage-rollup-v2` had a huge lag spike at 03:10 and then steady low throughput during replay.
sara: any DB errors in ETL?
eli: ETL pods show repeated failures when writing to `hourly_rollups`:
```
ERROR: could not obtain lock on relation "hourly_rollups"
DETAIL:  Process 31245 waits for ShareLock on transaction 5678; blocked by process 31260.
CONTEXT:  SQL statement "insert into hourly_rollups ..."
```
tim: repro I did locally against staging to mimic sequence: start backfill job that writes many tenant keys in parallel + run normal consumer. DB btree page locks escalated. Consumers began backing off with our retry policy and replayed slowly.
maria: hypothesis: backfill used high concurrency to speed up, but it hit hot hash partitions (same tenant/hour buckets) causing lock contention and vacuum churn. normal consumer got lock timeouts and exponential backoff => multi-hour lag.
sara: can we do quick mitigations? customers are asking for ETA.
eli: immediate plan: 1) pause the backfill job to stop introducing new lock pressure 2) relax consumer backoff and bump worker count so consumers can catch up once locks free 3) run targeted repair inserts for tenants still missing hours.
maria: commands I propose:
```bash
# pause backfill deployment
kubectl scale deployment backfill-runner -n analytics --replicas=0
# increase consumer workers
kubectl set env deployment/usage-rollup-v2 -n analytics CONSUMER_WORKERS=10
# short-term disable severe backoff
kubectl set env deployment/usage-rollup-v2 -n analytics CONSUMER_MAX_BACKOFF_MS=5000
```
eli: I'll pause the backfill now and watch consumer lag. pausing :arrow_down_small:
ingest-bot: alert muted for `usage-rollup-v2` for 2h while team mitigates
maria: writing repair SQL (run after locks clear) — sample for tenant `acme`:
```sql
insert into hourly_rollups (tenant_id, hour, tokens, updated_at)
select tenant_id, date_trunc('hour', event_time) as hour, sum(tokens), now()
from raw_events
where tenant_id = 'acme' and event_time >= '2024-05-01 00:00'
group by tenant_id, hour
on conflict (tenant_id, hour) do update set tokens = excluded.tokens, updated_at = excluded.updated_at;
```
sara: customer comms in progress: notified affected tenants, ETA 90min for partial catch-up, will update status page.
tim: follow-up action: we need a backfill safety check to avoid writing to hot partitions concurrently and add per-tenant rate limits to backfill tool (ticket INF-4219 created). also consider partition-aware batching to reduce lock collisions.
eli: after pausing backfill, consumer throughput improved and lag is dropping. 6/10 impacted tenants caught up within 45m.
maria: for remaining tenants, I'll run repair SQL after confirming no active locks.
sara: action items: eli — pause/monitor (in progress), maria — run repairs, tim — backfill safety ticket and throttle implementation, sara — customer updates. escalate to infra if DB lock timeouts persist.
eli: will post updates every 30m.
sara: thanks team, keeping thread for status. will close when all tenants <=5m lag.
